credit: Fundus Photo, Right Eye (OD)
description:
Fundus photograph of a healthy right eye (OD) from a myopic Asian male patient. Age 23. Notice the scleral and pigment crescents from 7 to 11 o'clock. The white glial tissue indicates a healthy nerve fiber layer above the retinal blood vessels. The margins of the small cup within the disc are indistinct and no lamina is visible. The macular region is clear and has a visible fovea.

description: Diabetic retinopathy is the most common cause of vision loss in working-age Americans. This condition damages the small blood vessels in the eye's light-sensitive retinal tissue. If these damaged blood vessels begin to leak near the center of the retina, known as the macula, the surrounding area swells and causes a condition called macular edema.~ National Institutes of Health

artist: Alexander M Balinski, Rachel N Harvey, Ryan B Ko, Melanie M Smalley, Nathan E Cutler, and Maham T Siddiqi
credit:
https://www.cureus.com/articles/98723-vaping-related-clotting-phenomena-presenting-as-central-retinal-vein-occlusion#!/

  • (5 August 2022). "Vaping-Related Clotting Phenomena Presenting As Central Retinal Vein Occlusion". Cureus. DOI:10.7759/cureus.27700. PMID 36081966. PMC: 9440988.
description: Figure 1: Fundoscopy demonstrating *dilated and tortuous venous vessels, †moderate dot/blot hemorrhages, and ‡Roth spots. A 23-year-old male presented to the emergency department with three weeks of intermittent left-sided eye pressure and vision loss in 2022. Upon further evaluation by a retina specialist, he was found to have multiple Roth spots and an impending central retinal vein occlusion in his left eye, accompanied by decreased visual acuity. After thorough exclusion of organic causes, his significant vaping history was considered the likely etiology of this hypercoagulable state and resultant central retinal vein occlusion.

commons_title: File:Retina photo of a right eye, patient with Severe Idiopathic Cranial Hypertension (aka Psuedotumor Cerebri).jpg
description: Photograph inside a human right eye of a patient suffering from the medical condition known as "Idiopathic Cranial Hypertension or Pseudo-tumor Cerebri". Which is a condition where pressure is extremely elevated in the brain (as if there is a tumor, but there is not) causing the Optic Nerve to swell,  protrude in to the eye, and slow important blood supply.
